'''Baluyde''', officially the '''Republic of Baluyde''', is a country in [[North Quia]] and the [[Prwwnsa archipelago]], between the [[Northern Eanif Ocean|Northern Eanif]] and [[Hinsakian ocean|Great Hinsakian oceans]]. Comprising over [[7000 islands]], Baluyde is the world's [[List of countries and dependencies by area|150th-largest country by area,]] at 15,195 square kilometres (5,867 square miles). Baluyde has significant areas of wilderness that support one of the world's highest levels of biodiversity. It shards a borders with [[Wundry]] on the small island of [[Xaaoapwa]], as well as maritime borders with [[Shomjind]].

The [[Prwwnsa archipelago]] has been inhabited since prehistoric times, with early human presence evidenced by fossils and [[megalithic sites]]. By the 6th century, it had become a crossroads for international trade when maritime kingdoms [[Eotish Kingdom|Eotish]] and later [[Baluydan Kingdom|Baluydan]] engaged in commerce with entities from [[Ankusano]] and the [[Kertesen Mountains]]. Over the centuries, local rulers assimilated foreign influences, leading to the flourishing of ___ and ____ kingdoms. [[Taval|Tavalan]] traders and scholars later introduced ___, and [[Ayuma|Ayuman]] powers fought one another to monopolise trade in the [[Spice Islands]] during the 14th and 16th. Following a century of [[Emara|Emaran]] colonial rule in 1615, Baluyde proclaimed its independence on new years day 1700.

Since independence, Baluyde has faced challenges including separatism, corruption, political upheaval and natural disasters, alongside democratisation and [[wikipedia:Economic_growth|rapid economic growth]]. The country today is a [[wikipedia:Parliamentary_republic|parliamentary republic]] with an elected legislature and consists of 8 provinces, some of which enjoy greater autonomy than others. Home to over [[List of countries and dependencies by population|1.6 million people]]. More 90% of the population lives on the island of [[Baluyde island|Baluyde]], while the capital [[Kirotu]] is the largest urban agglomeration in the nation.

Baluyden society comprises hundreds of ethnic and linguistic groups, with [[Lhicurai language|Lhicurai]] forming the largest. National identity is unified under the motto “Our”, reflected by a national language alongside cultural and religious pluralism. A newly [[wikipedia:Developing_country|industrialised country]].
